paperTitle: Comparative Study of FER Systems for Virtual Human Emotion Recognition
centralContribution: This research presents a comparative study of two pre-trained Facial Expression Recognition (FER) systems, FER library and Deepface, applied to emotion recognition in virtual humans, a task for which they were not originally designed. The study evaluates the systems' applicability across six emotional states and a neutral state, expanding FER system utility for validating 3D facial expressions in virtual humans and offering insights into their accuracy for pre-labelled emotions to potentially support facial animation.

units.title: Central Contribution
units.summary: Comparative study of FER systems for virtual human emotion recognition.

content.description: This research provides a comparative study of pre-trained Facial Expression Recognition (FER) systems (FER library and Deepface) when applied to emotion recognition in virtual humans, a novel application for these systems. The study evaluates their performance across six emotional states and a neutral state, thereby expanding the potential utility of FER systems for validating 3D facial expressions in virtual humans and offering crucial insights into their accuracy for pre-labelled emotions, which can support facial animation.

units.title: Abstract
units.summary: Summary of context, problem, approach, and gap in virtual human emotion recog...

content.description: The digital animation process, especially facial animation for virtual humans, is complex and demands significant expertise to achieve realism and avoid the 'Uncanny Valley.' Novice animators struggle with creating authentic facial expressions using morph targets. There is a clear need for a mechanism to quickly evaluate and validate these generated expressions. Existing FER systems are primarily designed for real human faces, leaving their reliability for virtual human emotion recognition unexplored. This study addresses this gap by evaluating the applicability of two pre-trained FER systems, FER library and Deepface, to virtual human emotion recognition, aiming to provide animators with a 'second opinion' or reference.

units.whyThisUnit: This stack groups all numerical and tabular data from the paper, providing detailed results and methodological insights.

content.description: This table presents the recognition accuracy of FER library and Deepface systems across different morph target activation intensities (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%). It shows increased accuracy as morph intensity rises.
content.title: Morph Intensity Impact on Recognition Accuracy

content.description: This table details the recognition accuracy of FER library and Deepface for seven emotional states. 'Happy' and 'neutral' are most recognized, while 'disgust' was not correctly identified by either system.
content.title: Emotion-Specific Recognition Performance

content.description: This table shows FER system face detection failures based on camera position. Frontal camera position resulted in significantly fewer failures, justifying its exclusive use for image capture.
content.title: FER System Face Detection Failures

content.description: This table shows FER system recognition accuracy across different virtual human ethnicities. Systems struggled more with darker skin tones and performed better with Caucasian and Asian characters.
content.title: FER Performance by Ethnicity

content.description: This table displays recalculated recognition accuracy for FER library and Deepface, considering only neutral and 75%+ morph levels. This adjusted view shows improved overall accuracy for both systems.
content.title: Recalculated Accuracy (75%+)
